eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 3, Lesson 18
subtitle: Walking every page of a real API without getting rate-limited.

code:
response = requests.get(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/pandas-dev/pandas/contributors",
    params={"per_page": 100, "page": 1},
)
page_1 = response.json()
print(len(page_1))
caption: per_page=100 is GitHub's max per request; page=2 would fetch the next 100 after that.
response.links is requests' parsed version of the Link header — when "next" disappears, you're on the last page.

eyebrow: A loop that walks every page
caption: No hardcoded page count, no guessing — it stops the moment "next" disappears from response.links.

code:
response = requests.get("https://api.github.com/repos/pandas-dev/pandas")

remaining = int(response.headers["X-RateLimit-Remaining"])
if remaining < 5:
    print("Getting close to the rate limit -- slow down or wait for reset.")
caption: Unauthenticated requests are capped at 60/hour per IP — go over it and GitHub returns a 403, not a crash.

subtitle: You've got clean, real data — now it's time for pandas.
